arxiv-1901-05161.title: On the Unbounded Picture of 𝑲 ​ 𝑲 \boldsymbol{KK} -Theory This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Noncommutative Manifolds and their Symmetries in honour of Giovanni Landi. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Landi.html
arxiv-1901-05161.creator: Jens KAAD
arxiv-1901-05161.description: Abstract In the founding paper on unbounded K ​ K KK -theory it was established by Baaj and Julg that the bounded transform, which associates a class in K ​ K KK -theory to any unbounded Kasparov module, is a surjective homomorphism (under a separability assumption).

arxiv-2011-04253.title: Machinery for Proving Sum-of-Squares Lower Bounds on Certification Problems
arxiv-2011-04253.creator: Aaron Potechin, Goutham Rajendran
arxiv-2011-04253.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Aaron Potechin, Goutham Rajendran. In this paper, we construct general machinery for proving Sum-of-Squares lower bounds on certification problems by generalizing the techniques used by Barak et al. [ BHK+16 ] to prove Sum-of-Squares lower bounds for planted clique. Using this machinery, we prove degree n ε n^{\varepsilon} Sum-of-Squares lower bounds for tensor PCA, the Wishart model of sparse PCA, and a variant of planted clique which we call planted slightly denser subgraph.

arxiv-2103-13226.title: Distributed Learning for Melanoma Classification using Personal Health Train
arxiv-2103-13226.creator: Yongli Mou, Sascha Welten, Yeliz Ucer Yediel, Toralf Kirsten, Oya Deniz Beyan
arxiv-2103-13226.description: Abstract TMF Workshop Usecase Implementation, Sep 2020 1 Introduction Skin cancer is the most common cancer type. Usually, patients with suspicion of cancer are treated by doctors without any aided visual inspection. At this point, dermoscopy has become a suitable tool to support physicians in their decision making.

arxiv-2111-13814.title: Enumerations of Universal Cycles for k k -Permutations
arxiv-2111-13814.creator: Zuling Chang, Jie Xue
arxiv-2111-13814.description: Abstract Universal cycle for k k -permutations is a cyclic arrangement in which each k k -permutation appears exactly once as k k consecutive elements. Enumeration problem of universal cycles for k k -permutations is discussed and one new enumerating method is proposed in this paper. Accurate enumerating formulae are provided when k = 2 , 3 k=2,3 .

arxiv-2207-10592.title: Quantum States of Fields for Quantum Split Sources
arxiv-2207-10592.creator: Lin-Qing Chen, Flaminia Giacomini, Carlo Rovelli
arxiv-2207-10592.description: Abstract Abstract: Field mediated entanglement experiments probe the quantum superposition of macroscopically distinct field configurations. We show that this phenomenon can be described by using a transparent quantum field theoretical formulation of electromagnetism and gravity in the field basis. The strength of such a description is that it explicitly displays the superposition of macroscopically distinct states of the field.

arxiv-2210-10633.title: Depth Contrast: Self-Supervised Pretraining on 3DPM Images for Mining Material Classification
arxiv-2210-10633.creator: Prakash Chandra Chhipa, Richa Upadhyay, Rajkumar Saini, Lars Lindqvist, Richard Nordenskjold, Seiichi Uchida, Marcus Liwicki
arxiv-2210-10633.description: Abstract This work presents a novel self-supervised representation learning method to learn efficient representations without labels on images from a 3DPM sensor (3-Dimensional Particle Measurement; estimates the particle size distribution of material) utilizing RGB images and depth maps of mining material on the conveyor belt. Human annotations for material categories on sensor-generated data are scarce and cost-intensive.

arxiv-2212-11218.title: Stochastic switching and squeeze of hysteresis window in nonlinear responses of silicon nitride membrane nanoelectromechanical resonators
arxiv-2212-11218.creator: Srisaran Venkatachalam, Xin Zhou
arxiv-2212-11218.description: Abstract In this work, we present the effects of stochastic force generated by white noise on the nonlinear dynamics of a circular silicon nitride membrane. By tuning the membrane to the Duffing nonlinear region, detected signals switching between low- and high-amplitudes have been observed.

arxiv-2303-04570.title: Braids and linked periodic orbits of disc homeomorphisms Thanks: Supported by NSF of China (No. 12071309)
arxiv-2303-04570.creator: Xiang LIU
arxiv-2303-04570.description: Abstract . This paper concerns on linked periodic orbits of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the 2 2 -disc in the sense of Gambaudo. We interpret the linking of periodic orbits by using their induced braids. Then based on the forcing relation of braids, we present a method for finding periodic orbits which are linked with a given one.

arxiv-2312-14058.title: Probing quantum properties of black holes with a Floquet-driven optical lattice simulator
arxiv-2312-14058.creator: Asmae Benhemou, Georgia Nixon, Aydin Deger, Ulrich Schneider, Jiannis K. Pachos
arxiv-2312-14058.description: Abstract In the curved spacetime of a black hole, quantum physics gives rise to distinctive effects such as Hawking radiation and maximally fast scrambling. Here, we present a scheme for an analogue quantum simulation of ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) and ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) -dimensional black holes using ultracold atoms in a locally Floquet-driven optical lattice.

arxiv-2405-18413.title: Homophily-adjusted social influence estimation
arxiv-2405-18413.creator: Hanh T.D. Pham, Daniel K. Sewell
arxiv-2405-18413.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hanh T.D. Pham, Daniel K. Sewell. Homophily and social influence are two key concepts of social network analysis. Distinguishing between these phenomena is difficult, and approaches to disambiguate the two have been primarily limited to longitudinal data analyses. In this study, we provide sufficient conditions for valid estimation of social influence through cross-sectional data, leading to a novel homophily-adjusted social influence model which addresses the backdoor pathway of latent homophilic features.

arxiv-2409-12271.title: On the Gravitational Wave Counterpart to a Gamma-ray Galactic Center Signal from Millisecond Pulsars
arxiv-2409-12271.creator: Kayla Bartel, Stefano Profumo
arxiv-2409-12271.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kayla Bartel, Stefano Profumo. The new tools of gravitational wave and multi-messenger astronomy allow for the study of astrophysical phenomenon in new ways and enables light to be shed on some of the longest-enduring mysteries of high-energy astrophysics. Among the latter stands the Galactic center gamma-ray excess, associated with a source whose nature could be annihilating dark matter or a yet-unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs).

arxiv-2411-07586.title: A Comprehensive Survey of AI-Driven Advancements and Techniques in Automated Program Repair and Code Generation
arxiv-2411-07586.creator: Avinash Anand, Nishchay Yadav, Akshit Gupta, Shaurya Bajaj
arxiv-2411-07586.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Avinash Anand, Nishchay Yadav, Akshit Gupta, Shaurya Bajaj. Bug fixing and code generation have been core research topics in software development for many years. The recent explosive growth in Large Language Models has completely transformed these spaces, putting in reach incredibly powerful tools for both. In this survey, 27 recent papers have been reviewed and split into two groups: one dedicated to Automated Program Repair (APR) and LLM integration and the other to code generation using LLMs.

arxiv-2504-11960.title: On Codes from Split Metacyclic Groups
arxiv-2504-11960.creator: Kirill Vedenev
arxiv-2504-11960.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kirill Vedenev. The paper presents a comprehensive study of group codes from non-abelian split metacyclic group algebras. We derive an explicit Wedderburn-like decomposition of finite split metacyclic group algebras over fields with characteristic coprime to the group order. Utilizing this decomposition, we develop a systematic theory of metacyclic codes, providing their algebraic description and proving that they can be viewed as generalized concatenated codes with cyclic inner codes and skew quasi-cyclic outer codes.

arxiv-2506-05941.title: Comparative Analysis of Modern Machine Learning Models for Retail Sales Forecasting
arxiv-2506-05941.creator: Luka Hobor, Mario Brcic, Lidija Polutnik, Ante Kapetanovic
arxiv-2506-05941.description: Abstract Accurate forecasting is key for all business planning. When estimated sales are too high, brick-and-mortar retailers may incur higher costs due to unsold inventories, higher labor and storage space costs, etc. On the other hand, when forecasts underestimate the level of sales, firms experience lost sales, shortages, and impact on the reputation of the retailer in their relevant market.

arxiv-2508-09998.title: INTIMA: A Benchmark for Human-AI Companionship Behavior
arxiv-2508-09998.creator: Lucie-Aimée Kaffee, Giada Pistilli, Yacine Jernite
arxiv-2508-09998.description: Abstract AI companionship, where users develop emotional bonds with AI systems, has emerged as a significant pattern with positive but also concerning implications. We introduce Interactions and Machine Attachment Benchmark (INTIMA), a benchmark for evaluating companionship behaviors in language models.

arxiv-2510-11945.title: Orbitally-Resolved Mechanical Properties of Solids from Maximally Localized Wannier Functions
arxiv-2510-11945.creator: Ethan T. Ritz, Guru Khalsa, Hsin-Yu Ko, Ju-an Zhang, Robert A. DiStasio Jr, Nicole A. Benedek
arxiv-2510-11945.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ethan T. Ritz, Guru Khalsa, Hsin-Yu Ko, Ju-an Zhang, Robert A. DiStasio Jr, Nicole A. Benedek. We present a technique for partitioning the total energy from a semi-local density functional theory calculation into contributions from individual electronic states in a localized Wannier basis.

pmc-10568728.creator: Seong-Joo Lee, Kwon Kyu Yu, Seong-min Hwang, Sangwon Oh, Nam Woong Song, Hak-Sung Jung, Oc Hee Han, Jeong Hyun Shim
pmc-10568728.description: Low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, conducted at or below a few millitesla, provides only limited spectral information due to its inability to resolve chemical shifts. Thus, chemical analysis based on this technique remains challenging. One potential solution to overcome this limitation is the use of isotopically labeled molecules.

pmc-10850672.title: Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 antibodies over 18 months following infection: UK Biobank COVID-19 Serology Study
pmc-10850672.creator: Jelena Bešević, Ben Lacey, Howard Callen, Wemimo Omiyale, Megan Conroy, Qi Feng, Derrick W Crook, Nicola Doherty, Daniel Ebner, David W Eyre, Dan Fry, Edward Horn, E Yvonne Jones, Brian D Marsden, Tim E A Peto, Fenella Starkey, David Stuart, Samantha Welsh, Natasha Wood, Alan Young, Allen Young, Mar
pmc-10850672.description: BackgroundLittle is known about the persistence of antibodies after the first year following SARS-CoV-2 infection. We aimed to determine the proportion of individuals that maintain detectable levels of SARS-CoV-2 antibodies over an 18-month period following infection.MethodsPopulation-based prospective study of 20 000 UK Biobank participants and their adult relatives recruited in May 2020.

pmc-11649790.title: Rainfall data modeling using improved adaptive type-II progressively censored Weibull-exponential samples
pmc-11649790.creator: Refah Alotaibi, Mazen Nassar, Ahmed Elshahhat
pmc-11649790.description: To get enough data from experiments that last for a long time, a recently unique improved adaptive Type-II progressive censoring technique has been suggested. This study, taking this scheme into consideration, concentrates on some conventional and Bayesian estimation tasks for parameter and reliability indicators, where the underlying distribution is the Weibull-exponential.

pmc-12537887.title: Epigallocatechin-gallate loaded BSA nanoparticles as innovative anti-inflammatory agents in immature macrophages
pmc-12537887.creator: Simona Martano, Mariafrancesca Cascione, Livia Giotta, Loris Rizzello, Riccardo Di Corato, Stefano Leporatti, Rosaria Rinaldi, Valeria De Matteis
pmc-12537887.description: IntroductionThe development of innovative anti-inflammatory therapies is critical for addressing chronic inflammatory diseases and cancer. Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a polyphenolic compound with strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, suffers from limited stability and bioavailability. Bovine Serum Albumin Nanoparticles (BSA-NPs), due to their biodegradability, non-toxicity, and high binding capacity, represent a powerful delivery system for bioactive compounds.

pmc-12773409.title: Abstract 108: Artery Of Percheron Infarctions (AOP): A Tale of Two Outcomes
pmc-12773409.creator: Eric N Beck, Nynoshka M Bassatt Cabrera, Melanie Ngo, Sherif Elwan, Claribel D Wee
pmc-12773409.description: IntroductionThe AOP is a rare anatomic variant in which a solitary arterial trunk arises from the proximal segment of the posterior cerebral artery (PCA) and supplies the bilateral paramedian thalami and rostral midbrain. Occlusion may result in variable bilateral thalamic and midbrain infarcts. The clinical presentation is most commonly lethargy and somnolence thought to lack other localizing features.

pmc-12822114.title: Co-delivery of camptothecin and SH3RF3-AS1 SiRNA for glioma synergistic therapy
pmc-12822114.creator: Shun Wang, Zhaochao Nie, Lei Liang, Jing Zou, Zhiyue Zhang, Donghai Wang, Chuncheng Qu, Cheng Wang, Jun Jiang
pmc-12822114.description: BackgroundCurrent treatment strategies for high-grade gliomas have a limited overall patient benefit. Here, Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) of glioma was conducted to screen the lncRNA regulated by m6A modification in glioma, and provide an innovative chemotherapeutic strategy to improved the therapeutic efficacy.

pmc-13326297.title: Predictive and discriminant validity of the Impaired Control Scale – Cannabis (ICS-C): an intensive longitudinal study of daily cannabis use outcomes
pmc-13326297.creator: Erin L Courtice, Nicolle Fox, Christian S Hendershot, Jeffrey D Wardell
pmc-13326297.description: Impaired control over substance use – difficulty adhering to limits on consumption – is a core feature of problematic use and addiction. Although extensively studied in alcohol research, impaired control over cannabis remains understudied. To advance research in this area, we evaluated the predictive and discriminant validity of the Impaired Control Scale–Cannabis (ICS-C) using an intensive longitudinal design.

pmc-13406702.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: High-Resolution Elucidation of Mitochondrial Dysregulation in Larval Zebrafish Gut
pmc-13406702.creator: Johanna A. Coetzee, Lesha Pretorius, Janica Theron, Angela Latakgomo, Carine Smith
pmc-13406702.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Mitochondrial dysfunction in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is multifactorial and not only linked to electron transport chain pathology.Mitochondrial morphometric abnormalities are illustrated in the ASD-like gut for the first time. What is the implication of the main findings? Consideration of the gut as part of a multicompartmental management approach is warranted in ASD.

pmc-13427534.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor Entitled “Critical Reappraisal of Obinutuzumab Randomized Trials in Membranous Nephropathy”
pmc-13427534.creator: Kajaree Giri, Richard J Glassock, Fernando C Fervenza
pmc-13427534.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). rimary membranous nephropathy (NCT04629248) a better comparison would have been against rituximab, the current standard of care. However, considering rituximab’s excellent response rates, to have a head-to-head study showing superiority of obinutuzumab versus rituximab, an end point required for US Food and Drug Administration approval, and assuming a complete remission rate of 35% in rituximab and 45% in obinutuzumab, would have required 1005 randomized patients (at 90% power for an absolute rate difference).

pmc-13521809.title: Intracranial Electrical Stimulation of the Superior Temporal Gyrus Evokes Rapid Responses in Human Visual Cortex
pmc-13521809.creator: Emily C. Cunningham, David Brang
pmc-13521809.description: Sounds can alter visual processing even at the earliest stages of the cortical pathway. However, our understanding of how acoustic signals are relayed to visual cortex is limited, particularly with respect to the involvement of different regions of auditory cortex in the most rapid stages of this communication across distinct visual areas.

pmc-13542428.title: Nasopharyngeal microbiome and resistome profiles in dairy calves fed milk replacer with low-level β-lactams
pmc-13542428.creator: Grazielle Cioletti, Sophia Kenney, Ernest Hovingh, Hayley Springer, Bradd J. Haley, Erika Ganda
pmc-13542428.description: Graphical AbstractSummary: Feeding waste milk to preweaning dairy calves is common practice, but concerns persist about its role in promoting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) due to the presence of antibiotic residues. This exploratory study investigated whether milk replacer supplemented with low levels of β-lactam antibiotics, simulating waste milk exposure, influences the nasopharyngeal microbiome and resistome of dairy calves.

pmc-13657618.title: Outcomes of sequential keratoplasty for bilateral gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy
pmc-13657618.creator: Mohammed M. Abusayf, Rana Alhumaemydi, Abeer Alkhodier, Majed AlKharashi
pmc-13657618.description: Rationale:Gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy (GDLD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by subepithelial amyloid deposition, progressive corneal opacification, and recurrent erosions. GDLD may present during the first decade of life and interfere with visual development. It may recur after keratoplasty, complicating surgical management.
